bull.b: Debt remains modest relative to equity, limiting balance-sheet strain while the company funds clinical development. This provides more financial flexibility than high-leverage peers, although it does not remove the need for future capital.

Net loss improved from roughly $30M in 2023–2024 to about $19M in 2025 and TTM. The direction indicates better cost control and could extend the runway if maintained, even though the company remains materially unprofitable during development.
Free cash flow improved from about $(24)M in 2023–2024 to $(12.7)M in 2025 and $(14.6)M TTM. Lower burn suggests a better spending trajectory, potentially slowing financing needs as programs advance.

bear.b: IN8bio reports zero revenue across annual periods and TTM, leaving no commercial revenue base to fund operations. As a clinical-stage biotech, it must develop candidates before recurring sales can support the business.

Operating cash flow and free cash flow were deeply negative in every period shown, and the company relies on external funding to sustain operations. Continued cash deficits can force additional financing while clinical programs remain underway.

Equity fell from about $38.2M in 2021 to $18.4M TTM, while total assets also declined. This capital erosion reflects cumulative losses and cash burn, reducing the financial cushion available to support development.
